questions.question: What does it mean for two sets $A$ and $B$ to have the same cardinality?
options: The sets have exactly the same elements.
There exists a bijection $f\colon A\to B$.
One set is a subset of the other.
There exists any function $f\colon A\to B$.

questions.question: For a finite set, what is its cardinality?
options: The largest element of the set.
The number of its distinct elements.
The number of possible subsets only.
The number of functions from the set to itself.

questions.question: What is the cardinality of the finite set $\{2,\,4,\,6\}$?
Which set has the same cardinality as $\{1,\,2,\,3\}$?
Cardinality compares the sizes of two sets by means of what?
options: Compare sets by the names of their elements.
Compare sets only by their smallest element.
Compare sets only when both are subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.

questions.question: How are finite sets classified by cardinality?
options: By whether their elements are ordered.

questions.question: Let $A = \{1,\,2\}$ and $B = \{x,\,y\}$. If $f(1) = x$ and $f(2) = y$, what does this show?
Suppose $|A| = |B|$ and $A$ is a finite set with five distinct elements. What can be concluded about $B$?
options: $B$ must contain the same elements as $A$.

questions.question: Can two infinite sets have different cardinalities?
options: All infinite sets have different cardinalities.
All infinite sets have the same cardinality.
Infinite sets may have equal or different cardinalities.
Infinite sets cannot be compared by cardinality.

questions.question: What is the cardinality of the empty set, $|\varnothing|$?
Although $\mathbb{N}\subsetneq\mathbb{Q}$, the two sets have the same cardinality. Which fact accounts for this?
options: Every rational number is a natural number.
There exists a bijection between $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$.

questions.question: Which example best illustrates that equal cardinality does not require equal elements?
Can an infinite set have the same cardinality as a proper subset of itself?
options: Yes; e.g. $\mathbb{N}$ and the even natural numbers
No; a proper subset is always strictly smaller

questions.question: Do $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{R}$ have the same cardinality?
options: No; R is strictly larger than N.

questions.question: What does cardinality measure?
options: The distance between two real numbers

questions.question: If $|A|=|B|$, does $|B|=|A|$ also hold?
A bijection witnessing $|A|=|B|$ must be:
options: A constant function (neither injective nor surjective in general).

questions.question: What is the cardinality of $\{1,1,2\}$ as a set?
Why are bijections central to cardinality?
options: They give one-to-one correspondences between sets.
They order elements from smallest to largest.
